mekki-muskil:205-205.t:
His saying {تضرعا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {وَالْآصَال}: the plural of أصل, and أصل is the plural of أصيل; it has also been said that الآصال is the plural of أصيل, which is the late afternoon (العشي). Abū Mijlaz read it with kasra on the hamza, making it the maṣdar of أصلنا, i.e. "we entered upon the late afternoon". So understand it, and you will be right, if Allah wills.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: Whoever puts {المص} in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), كتاب is its khabar (predicate). It is also possible to imply the khabar, and to put كتاب in the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying {وذكرى}: in the position of the nominative by conjunction to كتاب, or, if you wish, on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject). It may also be in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or by conjoining it to the position of the hāʾ in بِهِ. It has also been said that ذكرى is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to لتنذر, because its meaning is "the warning", so it is conjoined according to the meaning.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {قَلِيلا مَا تذكرُونَ} and {قَلِيلا مَا تؤمنون} and the like: it is accusative by the verb that follows it, and مَا is redundant (zāʾida). The basis of the accusative is that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverbial (ẓarf), its implied form being "a little remembering you remember" or "a little time you remember". If you take مَا with the verb as a maṣdar, it is not good to put قَلِيلا in the accusative by the verb that follows it, because you would be placing the ṣila before the relative (mawṣūl).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {وَكم من قَرْيَة}: كم is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the verb is occupied with the pronoun, namely أهلكناها, and what follows it is its khabar (predicate); and it is [the] declarative [كم] (khabariyya). It may also be in the position of the accusative by an implied verb after it, its implied form being "and how many a town We destroyed, We destroyed it". It is not permissible to assume the implied verb before it, because what precedes it does not govern it, owing to its resemblance to interrogative كم, and because it has the front of the sentence (ṣadr al-kalām), since it is the counterpart of رُبَّ, which also has the front of the sentence. The implied form of the verse is "and how many a town We willed to destroy, then Our punishment came to it", as He said فَإِذا قَرَأت الْقُرْآن فاستعذ بِاللَّه, that is, "when you intend to recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah".
His saying {بياتا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
And His saying {أَو هم قَائِلُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the ḥāl from الْقرْيَة.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as the predicate (khabar) of كَانَ, and دعواهم is the noun (ism). It is also possible for أَن to be in the position of the nominative as the noun of كَانَ, with دعواهم as the predicate placed first.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {وَالْوَزْن يَوْمئِذٍ الْحق}: الْحق is a naʿt (adjective) of الْوَزْن; الْوَزْن is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and يَوْمئِذٍ is its khabar (predicate). If you wish, you may make الْحق the khabar of الْوَزْن, with يَوْمئِذٍ as a non-predicative (mulghā) adverbial that you put in the accusative by الْوَزْن. It is also possible to put الْحق in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), with يَوْمئِذٍ as the khabar of الْوَزْن. If you make الْحق the khabar of الْوَزْن, you put يَوْمئِذٍ in the accusative as an adverbial of الْوَزْن, which governs it; or, if you wish, as an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and يَوْمئِذٍ is within the ṣila of the maṣdar in both of these aspects. If you make يَوْمئِذٍ the khabar of الْوَزْن, it is not within the ṣila, and it is accusative by an omitted element in whose place يَوْمئِذٍ stands, its implied form being "and the true weighing is established on that day" or "settled on that day", and the like. On this aspect it is good for الْحق to be a badal (substitute) from the pronoun that is in the adverbial, so it is not good to place it before the adverbial. If you make الْحق an adjective of الْوَزْن and the adverbial the khabar of الْوَزْن, it is permissible to place الْحق before the adverbial; and it is not permissible to place الْحق before الْوَزْن in either of the two aspects. If you make الْحق the khabar of الْوَزْن, it is permissible to place it before الْوَزْن, and not permissible to place it before the adverbial, because the adverbial is within the ṣila of الْوَزْن, and الْحق, which is the khabar of الْوَزْن, is not within its ṣila; and the ṣila is not separated from what it belongs to (the mawṣūl) by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His saying {معايش}: the plural of معيشة; its pattern is مفاعل, and the pattern of معيشة is مَفْعِلة. Its origin is مَعْيِشة; then the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred to the ʿayn, and the mīm is the augment, because it is from العيش. So it is not good to give it a hamza, because [the yāʾ] is a root letter whose origin in the singular is to be vowelled. Had it been an augment whose origin in the singular is to be vowelless, you would give it a hamza in the plural, as in سفائن, whose singular is سفينة on the pattern فعيلة, so the yāʾ is an augment whose origin is to be vowelless. Likewise you give it a hamza in the plural when the place of the yāʾ is an augmented alif or wāw, as in عَجَائِز and رسائل, because the singular is عَجُوز and رسالة. Khārija transmitted from Nāfiʿ the hamza in معايش (معائش); its justification is that he likened the root yāʾ to the augmented one and treated it in the same way, but this is far-fetched, and many of the grammarians do not permit it.
His saying {قَلِيلا مَا تشكرون}: like قَلِيلا مَا تذكرُونَ.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {إِلَّا إِبْلِيس}: accusative as an exception from outside the genus [of those excepted from]; it has also been said that it is from the genus.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {مَا مَنعك أَلا تسْجد}: مَا is an interrogative meaning denial (inkār), and it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). أَن is in the position of the accusative by مَنعك, as its object, and لَا is redundant (zāʾida). The implied form is "What thing prevented you from prostrating?" So in مَنعك there is an agent pronoun referring back to مَا. And إِذ is an adverb of past time, and what governs it is تسْجد.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {لأقعدن لَهُم صراطك}: that is, "on Your path" (على صراطك), in the same way as ضرب زيد الظّهْر والبطن ("Zayd was struck the back and the belly"), that is, on the back and the belly.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {مذؤوما مَدْحُورًا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in اخْرُج.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {فتكونا}: accusative as the answer to the prohibition.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَن تَكُونَا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "your Lord did not forbid you this tree except out of dislike that you become…" or "lest you become…". The hāʾ in هَذِه replaces a yāʾ and is for the feminine; because it replaces a yāʾ, what precedes it has a kasra, and it remains pronounced as hāʾ in continuous speech (waṣl). There is in the speech of the Arabs no feminine hāʾ preceded by a kasra, nor any feminine hāʾ that remains pronounced as hāʾ in continuous speech, other than this one; its origin is هاذي.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {لَكمَا لمن الناصحين}: the lām in لَكمَا is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "indeed I am an adviser to you, among the advisers". If you take the alif and lām in الناصحين as the definite article and not in the sense of الَّذِي, it is permissible for it to be attached to الناصحين; this is the view of al-Māzinī. In addressing the Lord, the dropping of يا has become frequent in the Qur'an. The reason for that is that in dropping يا from addressing the Lord, Exalted is He, there is the sense of glorifying Him and declaring Him transcendent. That is because the vocative carries something of the meaning of command: when you say يَا زيد, its meaning is "come, O Zayd; I call you, O Zayd". So يا was dropped from addressing the Lord so that the sense of command would disappear and be diminished, because يا strengthens it and makes its meaning manifest. In dropping يا there was glorification, exaltation and declaration of the Lord's transcendence; so its dropping became frequent in the Qur'an and in speech, in addressing the Lord, for that reason.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {وَإِن لم تغْفر لنا}: إن entered upon لم to return the verb to the original sense of its form, which is the future, because لم turns the imperfect to the sense of the past, and إن turns the past to the sense of the future. So when لم and the imperfect form after it came to mean the past, إن returned it to the future, because إن turns the past to the sense of the future.
His saying {جَمِيعًا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in اهبطا.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {بَعْضكُم لبَعض عَدو}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), also in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial); and likewise وَلكم فِي الأَرْض مُسْتَقر ومتاع إِلَى حِين.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying {ولباس التَّقْوَى}: whoever puts it in the accusative conjoins it to لِبَاس, which is accusative by أنزلنا. Whoever puts it in the nominative does so as a mubtadaʾ (subject), disjoined from what precedes it, with ذَلِك as its naʿt (adjective), or a badal (substitute) from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, and خير is its khabar (predicate). It is also possible to put لِبَاس in the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "and the covering of nakedness is the garment of التقوى", that is, of the God-fearing: he means "the garment of the people of التقوى", then the muḍāf was omitted. As for whoever puts لباس in the accusative, ذَلِك points to the garment or to all that preceded, and it is a mubtadaʾ with خير as its khabar — that is when you put لِبَاس التَّقْوَى in the accusative. The meaning of the verse in the nominative is: "and the garment of التقوى is better for you with Allah than the garment of clothes which are for adornment". And He said قد أنزلنَا عَلَيْكُم لباسا, meaning what We sent down of rain, by which flax and cotton grow, and by which the pasture grows that is the cause of the growth of wool, fur and hair on the backs of livestock. This sense is called "gradation" (al-tadrīj), because He, Exalted is He, named the thing by the name of what it proceeds from by stages. It has also been said, regarding لِبَاس التَّقْوَى in the reading of those who put it in the nominative, that it is the garment of wool and coarse cloth by which one humbles oneself before Allah the Exalted.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying {لَا يفتننكم}: its meaning is "stand firm in obedience to Allah and in turning back from disobedience to Him", like His saying فَلَا تموتن إِلَّا وَأَنْتُم مُسلمُونَ.
His saying {ينْزع عَنْهُمَا}: ينْزع is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in أخرج.
His saying {من حَيْثُ}: حَيْثُ is indeclinable (mabnī). It was made indeclinable only because it does not indicate a specific place, and because what follows it is part of its completion, like the ṣila and the relative. It was made indeclinable on a vowel because before its last letter there is a vowelless letter, and the ḍamma was most fitting for its vowel because it is a "limit" word (ghāya), so it was given the utmost of the vowels, which is the ḍamma, because it is the strongest of the vowels. It has also been said that it was made indeclinable on the ḍamma because its origin is حوث, so the ḍamma indicates the wāw. It may also take a fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying {مُخلصين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent nominative pronoun in ادعوه.
His saying {كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "you will return, a returning like His originating you". It has also been said that its implied form is "you will come forth, a coming-forth like His originating you".

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {فريقا هدى}: accusative by هدى. {وفريقا حق عَلَيْهِم الضَّلَالَة}: accusative by an implied verb in the sense of what follows it, its implied form being "and He led astray a party"; and on this implied form you pause at تعودُونَ. If you put فريقا and فريقا in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تعودُونَ, you do not pause at تعودُونَ but pause at الضَّلَالَة, the implied form being "as He originated you, you will return in this state". Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read تعودُونَ فريقين فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عَلَيْهِم الضَّلَالَة, and this shows that it is accusative as a ḥāl; so you do not pause at تعودُونَ when you put it in the accusative as a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا خَالِصَة}: whoever puts خَالِصَة in the nominative — and it is the reading of Nāfiʿ alone — puts it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "it is exclusive", and His saying للَّذين آمنُوا is then an explanation of the exclusiveness. It may also be a second khabar of هي, the meaning being "it will be exclusively for the believers on the Day of Resurrection". Whoever puts خَالِصَة in the accusative does so as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in الَّذين [i.e. للذين]; and what governs the ḥāl is the "settledness" and "establishment" in whose place للَّذين آمنُوا stands. For adverbials and prepositions govern ḥāls when they are predicates of a mubtadaʾ, because in them there is a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ, and because they stand in place of an omitted [word] running on the pattern of the verb, which is the real governor and the one in which the pronoun really lies. Do you not see that when you say زيد فِي الدَّار ("Zayd is in the house") and ثوب على زيد ("a garment is on Zayd"), its implied form is "Zayd is settled in the house" or "established in the house", and "a garment is settled" or "established on Zayd"? So in ثابت and مستقر there is a nominative pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ. When you omit ثابتا or مستقرا and make the adverbial or the preposition stand in its place, it stands in its place in governing, and the pronoun moves over and becomes implied and supposed in the adverbial and in the preposition — so understand it. The lām in للذين, and فِي in your saying فِي الدَّار, and على in your saying على زيد, are attached to that omitted element in whose place they stand. So the ḥāl is from that pronoun which moved over to the preposition, and what puts that pronoun in the nominative is what puts the ḥāl in the accusative. The implied form is: "Say: it is established for those who believe, in the state of its being exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection". Al-Akhfash said that His saying فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا is attached to His saying أخرج لِعِبَادِهِ, so أخرج governs the adverbial phrase فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا. It has also been said that His saying فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا is attached to حرم, so that governs it. So the meaning according to al-Akhfash is: "Say: who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants in the life of this world?"; and according to the view of the other: "Say: who has forbidden [in the life of this world] the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants?" It is not good for the adverbial phrase to be attached to زينة, because it has been qualified by an adjective, and neither the maṣdar nor the active participle governs once it is qualified, because it departs from resembling the verb, and because that would involve separating the ṣila from its relative: the governed element of the maṣdar is within its ṣila, while its adjective is not within its ṣila; so if you place the adjective before the governed element, you place what is not in the ṣila before what is in the ṣila. And in al-Akhfash's view there is a separation between the ṣila and the relative, because when he attaches the adverbial phrase to أخرج, it becomes part of the ṣila of الَّتِي, and it has been separated from الَّتِي by His saying والطيبات من الرزق قل هِيَ للَّذين آمنُوا, since what is conjoined to what precedes the ṣila and to the relative comes only after the relative is complete, while فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا is part of the completion of the relative; so part of the noun has been separated from [another] part by His saying والطيبات من الرزق قل هِيَ للَّذين آمنُوا. It is also possible for فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا to be attached to الطيبات من الرزق, so that the implied form is "and who has forbidden the good things of provision in the life of this world?" It is not good for فِي الْحَيَاة to be attached to الرزق, because you would have separated them by His saying قل هِيَ للَّذين آمنُوا. It is also possible for the adverbial phrase to be attached to آمنوا.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {مَا ظهر}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from الْفَوَاحِش.
His saying {وَأَن تُشْرِكُوا} and وَأَن تَقولُوا: أَن in both is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الْفَوَاحِش.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {إِمَّا يَأْتينكُمْ}: إمّا is a conditional particle, and the doubled nūn entered to emphasise the condition, because it is not an affirmed statement (ghayr wājib); and the verb with the nūn was made indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His saying {كلما}: accusative by لعنت, and it carries the sense of a condition.
His saying {اداركوا}: its origin is تداركوا on the pattern تفاعلوا; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, so the first of the assimilated pair became vowelless, and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was needed when beginning with it; so the alif remained in the script. It cannot be weighed on a pattern with the connecting alif, because you would be treating an augment as a root letter: you would say its pattern is افاعلوا, so that the tāʾ of تفاعلوا would become the fāʾ of the verb [i.e. the first root letter] because of its assimilation into the fāʾ of the verb, and that is not permissible. But if you weigh it according to the original form, it is permissible, and you say تفاعلوا.
His saying {جَمِيعًا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in اداركوا.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {وَمن فَوْقهم غواش}: غواش is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the prepositional phrase is its khabar (predicate). Originally it is a diptote, because it is on the pattern فواعل, the plural of غاشية; however, tanwīn entered it as a compensation for the yāʾ — and it has been said, as a compensation for the loss of the vowel of the yāʾ, and that is more correct. When two vowelless letters met — the yāʾ being vowelless and the tanwīn vowelless — the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the tanwīn came to follow the kasra that was before the dropped yāʾ. It has also been said: rather, it was simply dropped, and when the form fell short of فواعل, tanwīn entered it, so it became فواع, like جوار. This is its i'rab in the nominative and the genitive. When it is accusative, the yāʾ remains, with a fatḥa and without tanwīn, as in your saying رَأَيْت جواري, as a diptote.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {تجْرِي من تَحْتهم الْأَنْهَار}: تجْرِي is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in صُدُورهمْ.
His saying {لَوْلَا أَن هدَانَا الله}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, that is: "were it not that Allah's guidance of us is present" or "at hand, we would have perished" or "we would have been wretched". The lām and what follows it are the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْلَا.
His saying {أورثتموها}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from تلكم, I mean from the vague noun (al-mubham, i.e. the demonstrative). The kāf and mīm in تلكم are for address and have no grammatical position. Discussion of the noun [part] of تِلْكَ, its origin, what was dropped from it, and the lām has already preceded at His saying تِلْكَ الرُّسُل in [Surat] al-Baqara.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {أَن قد وجدنَا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by نادى, on the assumption of the omission of the preposition.
His saying {أَن لعنة}: whether one reads أَن light or with a shadda, its position is accusative by أذن or by مؤذن, on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, that is, بِأَن ("that…"); and there is an implied hāʾ [pronoun] when it is light. It is also possible, when it is light, for it to be in the sense of أَي, which is for explanation (tafsīr), so it has no grammatical position. Al-Aʿmash read it with a shadda and a kasra (إِنَّ), on the implication of the saying, that is: "and he said: indeed the curse of Allah…". بَينهم is an adverbial (ẓarf) governed by مؤذن or أذن. If you make بَينهم a naʿt (adjective) of مؤذن, that is permissible, but then مؤذن does not govern أَن, since it has been qualified by an adjective.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {يعْرفُونَ كلا}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رجال.
His saying {لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون}: if you take the meaning to be that they did enter, then وهم يطمعون is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent nominative pronoun in يدخلوها. Its meaning is that they had despaired of entering and had no hope of entering, yet they entered while in despair of that; that is, they did not enter it in a state of hoping to enter, but rather entered while in despair of entering. If you make its meaning that they have not yet entered it but hope to enter, the clause has no grammatical position, and its implied form is "they have not entered it, but they hope to enter by the mercy of Allah". This interpretation has been transmitted from the Companions and the Successors. It has also been said that طمع here has the sense of علم ("to know"), that is: "while they know that they will enter".

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {تِلْقَاء}: accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and the plural of تِلْقَاء is تلاقي.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {وَمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا}: مَا is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first مَا.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {هدى وَرَحْمَة}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the hāʾ in فصلناه, its implied form being "guiding and possessed of mercy". Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī permitted هدى وَرَحْمَة in the genitive, making them a badal (substitute) from علم; and هدى is also in the position of the genitive on this meaning. It is also possible to have وَرَحْمَة in the nominative, on the implication of "it is guidance and mercy".

mekki-muskil:53-53.t:
His saying {يَوْم يَأْتِي تَأْوِيله}: يَوْم is accusative by يقول.
His saying {أَو نرد}: nominative, conjoined to the interrogative, in the sense of "or will we be returned?", because the meaning of هَل لنا من شُفَعَاء is "will anyone intercede for us, or will we be returned?"; so you conjoin it according to the meaning.
His saying {فنعمل}: accusative because it is the answer to the wish (tamannī) with the fāʾ; it is accusative by an implied أَن, construed upon the maṣdar of what precedes it, so the fāʾ in meaning conjoins a maṣdar to a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t:
His saying {حثيثا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a swift pursuit". It may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "urging on".
His saying {وَالشَّمْس وَالْقَمَر}: conjoined to السَّمَوَات. Whoever reads it in the nominative does so as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with مسخرات as the khabar (predicate). Likewise whoever reads والنجوم in the nominative in [Surat] al-Naḥl: it is nominative by disjunction (qaṭʿ) and as a mubtadaʾ, with مسخرات as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t:
His saying {تضرعا وخفية}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "possessed of humility".
His saying {إِن رَحْمَة الله قريب} [Translator's note: this is 7:56]: قريب is masculine because الرَّحْمَة and الرحم are the same, so it is construed according to the meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: قريب came without hāʾ only to distinguish between قريب in kinship and قريب in nearness. Abū ʿUbayda said: قريب is masculine on the basis of the masculinity of "place", that is, "a near place". Al-Akhfash said: الرَّحْمَة here is the rain, so it is made masculine according to the meaning. It has also been said that it is masculine by way of relation (nasab), that is, "possessed of nearness".
His saying {نشرا} [Translator's note: this is 7:57]: whoever reads the nūn with a fatḥa (نَشْرا) makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl. Whoever reads the nūn and the shīn with a ḍamma (نُشُرا) makes it the plural of نشور, intended in the sense of an active participle, like طهور in the sense of طاهر — as though the wind were "reviving" (nāshira) the earth, that is, giving it life, since it brings the rain. It may also be the plural of نشور in the sense of a passive participle, like ركوب and حلوب — as though Allah gave it life so that it may bring the rain. It has also been said that it is the plural of ناشر, like قاتل and قتل. The same is said of the reading of whoever reads the nūn with a ḍamma and the shīn vowelless (نُشْرا), for lightness. It has also been said that whoever reads the nūn with a fatḥa and the shīn vowelless [is reading] a maṣdar in the manner of كتاب الله, in which the sense of the speech operates. As for whoever reads it with a bāʾ with a ḍamma (بُشْرا), it is the plural of بشير as بُشُر, then the shīn was made vowelless for lightness — the plural of فعيل on فُعُل — and it is also accusative as a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {إِلَّا نكدا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يخرج. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense of "possessed of meagreness". Likewise it is a maṣdar on the reading of Abū Jaʿfar with a fatḥa on the kāf (نَكَدا). Ṭalḥa read it with the kāf vowelless (نَكْدا), for lightness, just as one lightens كَتِف (to كَتْف).

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {من إِلَه غَيره}: whoever reads غير in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of إله according to its position, or makes غير in the sense of إِلَّا and gives it the i'rab of what comes after إِلَّا in this position, which is the nominative as a badal (substitute) from إله according to the position — as He said وَمَا من إِلَه إِلَّا الله, putting it in the nominative as a badal from the position of إله; and likewise لا إله إلا الله: [الله is] a badal from إله according to the position. And لكم is the khabar (predicate) of إله. It is also possible to imply the khabar, its implied form being "you have no god other than Him in existence" or "in the world", and the like. The genitive in غير is as an adjective according to the form [of إله]; it is not permissible as a badal according to the form, just as it would not be permissible for مِن to enter [the badal] if you deleted the substituted noun, because it does not enter in an affirmative statement.
His saying {آلَاء الله} [Translator's note: this is 7:69]: the singular of آلَاء is إلى, or ألى, or إلي, or إلَيّ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant singulars is uncertain in the text], in the same way as the singular of آنَاء اللَّيْل.

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His saying {وَإِلَى عَاد أَخَاهُم هودا} and {وَإِلَى ثَمُود أَخَاهُم صَالحا}: all of it is conjoined to أرسلنا in His saying أرسلنَا نوحًا, that is: "and We sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ, and to ʿĀd their brother Hūd, and to Madyan their brother Shuʿayb". Likewise ولوطا: its implied form is "and We sent Lūṭ"; and, if you wish, you may put it in the accusative in the sense of "and remember Lūṭ".

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَن يَشَاء الله}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); it has also been said that its implied form is "except by the will of Allah".

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His saying {أَن لَو نشَاء}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of يهد. Mujāhid read نهد with nūn, and on his reading أَن is in the position of the accusative by نهد.

mekki-muskil:102-102.t: His saying {وَإِن وجدنَا أَكْثَرهم لفاسقين}: according to Sībawayh, إِن is lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and the lām became obligatory in its predicate as compensation for the doubling. It has also been said that the lām became obligatory to distinguish between the إِن lightened from the heavy and إِن when it is in the sense of مَا. The Kufans said: إِن is in the sense of مَا and the lām in the sense of إِلَّا, its implied form being "and We found most of them nothing but transgressors".

mekki-muskil:105-105.t: His saying {أَن لَا أَقُول}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being بِأَن لَا ("that … not"); or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what precedes it as its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:107-107.t: His saying {فَإِذا هِيَ ثعبان}: إِذا is for surprise (mufājaʾa), in the same way as your saying خرجت فَإِذا زيد قَائِم ("I went out, and lo, Zayd was standing"). It is also permissible to put ثعبان and قائم in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with إِذا as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject). The إِذا of surprise, according to al-Mubarrad, is an adverb of place; that is why it may be a predicate of concrete things (al-juthath). Others said: it is an adverb of time, as it is elsewhere in speech; but when you say خرجت فَإِذا زيد, its implied form is "and lo, the occurrence of Zayd" or "the presence of Zayd", or similar maṣdars; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was made to stand in its place, just as you say اللَّيْلَة الْهلَال ("tonight the new moon"), that is, the appearance of the new moon is tonight, then it was omitted on that assumption; and adverbs of time can be predicates of maṣdars. Similar to it is فَإِذا هِيَ بَيْضَاء للناظرين [Translator's note: 7:108].

mekki-muskil:110-110.t: His saying {فَمَاذَا تأمرون}: مَا is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ذَا has the sense of الَّذِي and is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and there is a hāʾ omitted from the ṣila, its implied form being "so what is it that you command [concerning it]?" It is also possible to make مَا and ذَا a single noun in the position of the accusative by تأمرون, without implying an omitted element.

mekki-muskil:115-115.t:
His saying {إِمَّا أَن تلقي وَإِمَّا أَن نَكُون}: أَن is in the position of the accusative in both according to the Kufans, as though he said "either you do the casting" [Translator's note: the text reads إِمَّا أَن تفعل إِلَّا لِقَاء, evidently a corruption of إمّا أن تفعل الإلقاء], as the poet said:
... قَالُوا الرّكُوب فَقُلْنَا تِلْكَ عادتنا ... أَو تَنْزِلُونَ فَإنَّا معشر نزل ...
(They said: "Riding!" We said: "That is our custom — or will you dismount? For we are a people who dismount [to fight].")
so he put الرّكُوب in the accusative. Some grammarians permitted أَن to be in the position of the nominative, in the sense of "either it is the casting" [Translator's note: the text reads إِمَّا هُوَ الا لِقَاء, evidently for إمّا هو الإلقاء]. His saying أَن {ألق} [Translator's note: 7:117]: أَن is in the position of the accusative, that is, بِأَن ألق ("that: cast"); it may also be explicative (tafsīr), in the sense of أَي, so that it has no grammatical position.

mekki-muskil:132-132.t: His saying {مهما}: it is a conditional particle, and its origin is مَا مَا: the first مَا is for the condition and the second is emphasis. Two particles of the same wording were felt to be heavy, so they replaced the alif of the first مَا with hāʾ. It has also been said that it is مَه, which is for rebuke, entered upon conditional مَا, and the two were made a single word. Ibn al-Anbārī reported مهمن يكرمني أكْرمه ("whoever honours me, I will honour him"), and said: the origin is مَن مَن يكرمني, the second مَن being emphasis in the same way as مَا; so the nūn of the first مَن was replaced by hāʾ, just as they replaced the alif of the first مَا with hāʾ in مهما. That is because مَا and مَن are kindred in [many] things, even if they differ in one thing; so the occurrence of the word مَن twice together was disliked, just as that was disliked with مَا.

mekki-muskil:133-133.t:
His saying {الطوفان}: it is the plural of طوفانة; it has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like النقصان. As for الْجَرَاد, its singular is جَرَادَة, which applies to male and female, and no distinction is made between them: you say رَأَيْت جَرَادَة ذكرا أَو أُنْثَى ("I saw a locust, male or female").
His saying {آيَات مفصلات}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what precedes it, and مفصلات is a naʿt (adjective) of الآيات.

mekki-muskil:135-135.t: His saying {هم بالغوه}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of أجل.

mekki-muskil:137-137.t:
His saying {الَّتِي باركنا فِيهَا}: الَّتِي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of المشارق and المغارب, and مشارق is the second object of أورثنا. It is also possible for الَّتِي to be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of الأرض. It is also possible for الَّتِي to be the naʿt of an omitted second object of أورثنا, its implied form being "and We caused the people who were [oppressed] to inherit the land which We blessed", so that مشارق and مغارب are two adverbials of the oppression (al-istiḍʿāf); but this is far-fetched and is only permissible on the omission of the preposition. The hāʾ in فِيهَا refers back to المشارق and المغارب, or to الأرض, or to الَّتِي when you make it the naʿt of the omitted الأرض.
His saying {ودمرنا مَا كَانَ يصنع فِرْعَوْن}: in كَانَ is its noun (ism) [Translator's note: the text reads اسمهما, "their noun"; evidently اسمها is meant], referring back to مَا, and the clause is its predicate (khabar). The hāʾ is omitted from يصنع, referring back to the noun of كَانَ, which is the pronoun of مَا. It has also been said that كَانَ is redundant (zāʾida). Some of the Basrans permitted فِرْعَوْن to be the noun of كَانَ, intended to come first, with يصنع as the predicate; but this is far-fetched. Likewise he said regarding His saying وَإنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُول سفيهنا على الله that سفيهنا is the noun of كَانَ. Most of the Basrans do not permit it, because the second verb has a better claim to put the noun after it in the nominative than the first verb. Whoever permits this would be bound to permit يقوم زيد as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) with fronting and postponement, and no one has permitted that.

mekki-muskil:138-138.t:
His saying {أصنام لَهُم}: لَهُم is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أصنام.
His saying {إِلَهًا} [Translator's note: this is 7:140], the second: accusative as a clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), because أبغيكم has already passed to two objects, غير and the kāf and mīm.

mekki-muskil:141-141.t:
His saying {يسومونكم}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from آل فِرْعَوْن.
And His saying {يقتلُون}: a badal (substitute) from يسومونكم, or a ḥāl from the latent nominative pronoun in يسومونكم.

mekki-muskil:142-142.t:
His saying {ثَلَاثِينَ لَيْلَة}: that is, "the completion of thirty nights" or "the passing of thirty nights". It is not good to put ثلاثين in the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf) of the promise, because the promise did not take place during them; so it is the second object of وعد, on the assumption of the omission of the muḍāf and the placing of the muḍāf ilayhi in its place.
His saying {فتم مِيقَات ربه أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَة}: He repeated the mention of forty for emphasis. It has also been said: so that it would be known that the ten are nights and not hours. And it has been said: so that it would be known that the thirty were completed without the ten, since it would be possible that the thirty were only completed with the ten; so He repeated the mention of the forty so that it would be known that the ten are other than the thirty. الأربعون is accusative as being in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He said: "so the appointed term of his Lord was completed, numbered as forty nights", or "measured at this measure".

mekki-muskil:143-143.t:
His saying {دكا}: whoever reads it with prolongation (دَكَّاءَ) does so on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, that is, "like a دكاء land", and the دكاء land is the level one. It has also been said: "like a دكاء she-camel", which is the one that has no hump, level in the back. Its meaning is: He made it level with the ground, with no elevation above the ground. It is a diptote because, like حمراء, it contains the alif of the feminine and is an adjective, and those are two causes. Whoever gives it tanwīn and does not prolong it (دَكًّا) makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of دككت الأَرْض دكا, that is, "I made it level". Al-Akhfash said: it is an object, and there is also an omitted muḍāf in it, because the verb before it, namely جعله, is not from its root; and its implied form is "and He made it possessed of levelling", that is, possessed of levelness.
His saying {صعقا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مُوسَى.

mekki-muskil:145-145.t: His saying {فَخذهَا}: its origin is فَأَخذهَا, and the origin of خُذ is أؤخذ, but it is not used in its original form; it was shortened for lightness because of the combination of ḍammas, the wāw and the guttural letter. They have said اؤمر and اؤخذ, using it in its original form; and of this is His saying وَأمر أهلك [Translator's note: 20:132]; had it been used in the lightened form, He would have said وَمر أهلك, which is permissible in speech.

mekki-muskil:148-148.t: His saying {من حليهم}: its origin is من حلويهم, the plural of حلي — فَعْل on فُعُول, like كعب and كعوب. Then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ after giving a kasra to what precedes it, which is the lām, so that the vowellessness of the yāʾ would be sound, and the ḥāʾ kept its ḍamma (حُلِيّهم). Whoever gives it a kasra (حِلِيّهم) makes it follow the kasra of the lām.

mekki-muskil:150-150.t: His saying {قَالَ ابْن أم}: whoever reads the mīm with a fatḥa makes the two nouns a single noun, like خمسة عشر, and the fatḥa on ابن is one of indeclinability (bināʾ), not of i'rab, like the tāʾ of خمسة عشر and like the fatḥa in رويدك when you intend the imperative in the sense of أرود. It has also been said that the origin is ابن أما, then the alif was dropped; but that is far-fetched, because the alif is a compensation for a yāʾ, and the dropping of the yāʾ only happens in the vocative, and أم is not the one addressed. Whoever reads the mīm with a kasra annexes ابن to أم, and the fatḥa of ابن is a fatḥa of i'rab, because it is an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf).

mekki-muskil:155-155.t: His saying {وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قومه سبعين رجلا}: قومه and سبعين are the two objects of اختار, and قومه is accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition from it, that is, "from his people" (من قومه).

mekki-muskil:160-160.t: His saying {اثْنَتَيْ عشرَة أسباطا}: it was made feminine only on the assumption of an omitted أمة ("community"), its implied form being "twelve communities". أسباط is a badal (substitute) from اثنتي عشرة, and أمم is a naʿt (adjective) of أسباط.

mekki-muskil:163-163.t:
His saying {إِذْ يعدون}: what governs إِذْ is سل ("ask"), its implied form being "ask them about the time of their transgressing in the Sabbath".
His saying {شرعا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الحيتان. The most eloquent usage is to put the adverbial in the accusative with السبت and الجمعة, so you say اليوم السبت and اليوم الجمعة, putting اليوم in the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), because السبت and الجمعة carry the sense of a verb, since السبت means "rest" and الجمعة means "gathering"; so you put اليوم in the accusative as an adverbial. With the rest of the days you use the nominative, so we say اليوم الأحد and اليوم الأربعاء, because there is no verbal sense in them, so the mubtadaʾ (subject) is the khabar (predicate), and you put both in the nominative.

mekki-muskil:164-164.t: His saying {قَالُوا معذرة}: whoever puts it in the accusative does so as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and whoever puts it in the nominative does so as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject). Sībawayh preferred the nominative, because they did not mean to excuse themselves from a matter for which blame was due upon them; rather it was said to them "Why do you admonish?", and they said: "the matter of our admonition is an excuse".

mekki-muskil:165-165.t: His saying {بِعَذَاب بئيس}: whoever reads it with yāʾ without hamza (بِيس), its origin is بَئِس on the pattern فَعِل; then the hamza was made vowelless — a dialectal usage with a guttural letter when it is the ʿayn [middle radical] — after the bāʾ had been given a kasra to follow the kasra of the hamza, by assimilation (itbāʿ), as they say شَهِد, شِهِد and شِهْد; then the hamza was replaced by yāʾ. It has also been said that it is a past verb transferred to naming and then used as a description, like what is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids قيل وقال (gossip: 'it was said' and 'he said')". So the origin of the yāʾ is a hamza, and its origin is بئس like علم; then the bāʾ was given a kasra by assimilation, then made vowelless according to the dialect of those who say عِلْم for عَلِم, then the hamza was replaced by yāʾ. As for whoever reads it with the hamza on فَعِيل (بَئِيس), he makes it the maṣdar of بئس يبأس; Abū Zayd reported بئس يبأس بئيسا, so it is like النذير and النكير; and the implied form on this is "with a punishment possessed of بئس", that is, possessed of misery (بؤس). As for whoever reads it on فَيْعَل (بَيْأَس), he makes it an adjective of العذاب, like ضيغم. A kasra on the hamza on فَيْعِل (بَيْئِس) has been transmitted from ʿĀṣim, but it is far-fetched, because this form only occurs with verbs whose ʿayn is weak, like سيد and ميت. In this word there are anomalous (shādhdh) readings other than those we mentioned, whose explanation would be lengthy.

mekki-muskil:170-170.t: His saying {إِنَّا لَا نضيع أجر المصلحين}: its implied form is "[the reformers] among them", so that a resumptive element (ʿāʾid) from its khabar (predicate) refers back to the mubtadaʾ (subject), which is وَالَّذين يمسكون.

mekki-muskil:171-171.t: His saying {كَأَنَّهُ ظلة}: the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الجبل. It has also been said that the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is as though it were a canopy". And إِذ is in the position of the accusative by an implied اذكر ("remember"); and similar to it is وَإِذ أَخذ رَبك.

mekki-muskil:172-172.t:
His saying {من ظُهُورهمْ}: a badal (substitute) from بني آدم with the repetition of the preposition, and it is a badal of part for whole. We have mentioned the ruling on بلى, its reasons, the origin of its alif, the difference between it and نعم, their meaning and their use in speech, in the Book of كلا.
His saying {أَن تَقولُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:177-177.t: His saying {سَاءَ مثلا الْقَوْم}: in سَاءَ there is an agent pronoun, مثلا is a specification (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)), and الْقَوْم is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what precedes them as their khabar (predicate); or nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "evil is the example as an example; they are the people who…", like نعم رجلا زيد ("an excellent man is Zayd"). Al-Akhfash said: its implied form is "evil as an example is the example of the people".

mekki-muskil:185-185.t:
His saying {وَأَن عَسى}: أَن is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ملكوت.
His saying {عَسى أَن يكون}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by عسى.

mekki-muskil:186-186.t: His saying {ويذرهم}: whoever reads it in the nominative disjoins it from what precedes it. Whoever reads it in the jussive conjoins it to the position of the fāʾ in His saying فَلَا هادي لَهُ, because it is in the position of the jussive, since it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

mekki-muskil:187-187.t:
His saying {أَيَّانَ مرْسَاها}: مرسى is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أيان is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. It is an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and it was made indeclinable only because it carries the meaning of interrogation.
His saying {إِلَّا بَغْتَة}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:188-188.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ الله}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

mekki-muskil:189-189.t: His saying {آتيتنا صَالحا}: صَالحا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a sound giving".

mekki-muskil:190-190.t:
His saying {جعلا لَهُ شُرَكَاء}: that is, "possessor of partnership" or "possessors of partnership"; this goes back to the reading of whoever reads شُرَكَاء as the plural of شريك. If the omission is not assumed in it, that would not be a censure of the two of them, because the meaning would become that they assigned to Allah a share of what He gave them of wealth, crops and the like, and that is praise. If you do not assume the omission of a muḍāf at the end of the phrase, you assume it at the beginning of the phrase; one of the two aspects is unavoidable. In the reading of whoever reads شركا on the pattern فِعْل, its implied form is "they assigned to other than Him a share"; if you do not assume an omission, the meaning is inverted and the censure becomes praise — so understand it.
Ibn Jubayr read {إِن الَّذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم} [Translator's note: 7:194] with عبادًا and أمثالَكم in the accusative and إن light, making it in the sense of مَا, so it puts [the words] in the accusative as its predicate. Sībawayh prefers, with the lightened إن that is in the sense of مَا, the nominative for the predicate, because it is weaker than مَا; while al-Mubarrad treats it as مَا is treated.
His saying {طيف} [Translator's note: 7:201]: whoever reads it on the pattern فَعْل makes it the maṣdar of طاف يطيف. It has also been said that it is lightened from طيّف, like ميت from ميّت.
